title: Uncovering the Turing Test's Latent Signal: Indistinguishability as a Reward
abstract: arXiv:2610.34781v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Can a model learn by trying to fool another model? We show that it can. Inspired by the Turing Test and its recent generalization to arbitrary distinguishers, we introduce a domain-based teacher-Turing-Test, in which a stronger teacher model serves as both the target of imitation and the distinguisher, and a weaker student model is trained to make the teacher attribute responses to itself. We use this self-attribution (or fooling) probability as a reinforcement learning reward, without ever providing the student ground-truth answers, nor requiring the teacher to generate responses. We test our approach independently in four domains with verifiable answers: CommonsenseQA (reasoning), GSM8K (mathematics), KodCode (programming), and Spider (SQL), training a Qwen2.5-1.5B student/imitator model using DeepSeek V4 Flash as teacher/distinguisher. translated_title: 揭示图灵测试的潜在信号：将不可区分性作为奖励
translated_abstract: 一个模型能否通过试图欺骗另一个模型来学习？我们证明它可以。受图灵测试及其近期向任意判别器的推广所启发，我们提出了一种基于领域的“教师-图灵测试”框架：更强的教师模型同时充当模仿目标与判别器，而较弱的学生模型则被训练以让教师将回答归因于它自己。我们将这种自我归因（即“欺骗”）概率用作强化学习的奖励信号，既无需向学生提供真实标准答案，也无需教师生成回答。我们在四个具有可验证答案的领域独立测试了该方法：CommonsenseQA（推理）、GSM8K（数学）、KodCode（编程）和 Spider（SQL），使用 DeepSeek V4 Flash 作为教师/判别器，训练 Qwen2.5-1.5B 的学生/模仿者模型。除了在通过图灵测试方面有所提升外，学生在独立的保留评估集上也取得了进步……
tldr: 该论文提出以图灵测试中的“不可区分性”（欺骗强教师模型的自我归因概率）作为强化学习奖励，使弱学生模型在无需真实答案、无需教师生成回答的情况下，在推理、数学、编程和SQL等多个领域获得性能提升。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes using indistinguishability—the probability of fooling a stronger teacher in a Turing Test—as a reinforcement learning reward, enabling a weaker student model to improve across reasoning, math, coding, and SQL tasks without ground-truth answers or teacher-generated responses.
